config.title: auto-fit and minmax()

intro.title: auto-fit and minmax()
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a responsive grid layout that automatically adjusts the number of columns based on the available screen width. You will learn to use the CSS Grid properties auto-fit and minmax() to create flexible, fluid grids without media queries. The core concept involves defining a grid with columns that have a minimum size but can expand to fill the space, with auto-fit handling the column count dynamically. You'll work with CSS Grid syntax, specifically the repeat() function combined with these properties. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you create layouts that look great on any device.
intro.usecase: The auto-fit and minmax() functions are essential for creating responsive grid layouts that adapt to different screen sizes. You'll use this pattern in product dashboards where card-based content needs to rearrange itself automatically as users resize their browser windows. E-commerce sites employ these functions to display product grids that maintain minimum card widths while filling available space efficiently. News websites use auto-fit with minmax() to create flexible article layouts that work seamlessly on mobile, tablet, and desktop devices without media query clutter.

objectives: Implement a CSS Grid layout using the repeat() function with auto-fit
Configure responsive grid columns that adjust automatically to container width
Apply the minmax() function to define flexible column size constraints
Construct grid layouts that maintain minimum column widths while expanding to fill available space
Manipulate grid column behavior by combining auto-fit with minmax() parameters
Update existing grid layouts to incorporate responsive auto-fit functionality
Control grid item distribution across varying viewport sizes using auto-fit and minmax()

steps.title: Create a CSS file and add a container with display: grid
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and define a .container class with display: grid to establish a grid layout context
steps.hint: Start by creating a CSS rule for a class named 'container' and set its display property to 'grid'.
steps.seedCode: /* Create a .container class with display: grid */
steps.expectedOutcome: A .container class is defined with display: grid, setting up the foundation for a grid layout.
successCriteria: The .container class is defined with display: grid property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined the .container class with display: grid.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container class with display: grid is not properly defined. Check that you've created a CSS rule for .container with display: grid.

steps.title: Add grid-template-columns with fixed pixel values
steps.instruction: Add the property grid-template-columns: 100px 100px 100px; to the .container class to create three equal fixed-width columns.
steps.hint: Inside the .container rule, add a new line with grid-template-columns: 100px 100px 100px; after the display: grid; property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container class will have a grid layout with three columns, each exactly 100 pixels wide.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added grid-template-columns: 100px 100px 100px; to the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-columns property is missing or incorrect. Add grid-template-columns: 100px 100px 100px; to the .container class.

steps.title: Replace fixed values with repeat() function
steps.instruction: In the .container rule, replace the current grid-template-columns with `repeat(3, 100px)` to create three 100px columns using the repeat() function.
steps.hint: The repeat() function takes two arguments: the number of repetitions and the size of each column. Use it to simplify your grid definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid will have three columns, each 100px wide, defined more efficiently with repeat().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the exact syntax `repeat(3, 100px)` inside the grid-template-columns property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-columns property should be set to `repeat(3, 100px)` to create three 100px columns using the repeat() function.

steps.title: Introduce the minmax() function
steps.instruction: Inside the .container rule, replace the fixed pixel value in the repeat() function with minmax(100px, 200px) to create flexible columns.
steps.hint: Update grid-template-columns to use repeat(3, minmax(100px, 200px)). This makes each column at least 100px wide but can grow up to 200px.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid columns will now have flexible widths between 100px and 200px, instead of fixed 100px widths.
successCriteria: The grid-template-columns property uses repeat(3, minmax(100px, 200px)).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using minmax(100px, 200px) inside the repeat() function for grid-template-columns.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced the fixed pixel value with minmax(100px, 200px) inside the repeat() function.

steps.title: Add auto-fit keyword to the repeat() function
steps.instruction: In the .container rule, replace the fixed number '3' in the repeat() function with the keyword 'auto-fit' to make the grid responsive.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid will now automatically create as many columns as can fit in the container width, each 100px wide.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you replaced '3' with 'auto-fit' inside the repeat() function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you changed 'repeat(3, 100px)' to 'repeat(auto-fit, 100px)' in the .container rule.

steps.title: Add grid items to visualize the layout
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a .grid-item class with basic styling to create visible grid cells. Include background color, padding, and border properties.
steps.hint: Define .grid-item with properties like background-color, padding, and border to make the grid cells stand out visually.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .grid-item class is defined with styling that makes grid cells visible when HTML elements with that class are added later.
successCriteria: The .grid-item rule includes background-color, padding, and border properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include all three: background-color, padding, and border.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .grid-item class is missing or doesn't have the required styling properties.

steps.title: Add gap property to create space between grid items
steps.instruction: Add a gap property to the .container class to create consistent spacing between grid items. Set the gap to 10px.
steps.hint: Use the CSS property 'gap' to add spacing between grid rows and columns.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have 10px spacing between all grid items.
successCriteria: The .container class includes a gap property set to 10px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the gap property to the .container class with a value of 10px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gap property is missing or incorrect. Add 'gap: 10px;' to the .container class.

steps.title: Test the responsive behavior by adjusting container width
steps.instruction: Add a fixed width property to the .container class to test how auto-fit and minmax() respond to different container sizes.
steps.hint: Set a width like 500px or 80% on the .container rule to see how the grid columns rearrange.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have a defined width, allowing you to observe how auto-fit and minmax() create responsive columns that adjust to the available space.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes a width property with a fixed value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you add the width property directly to the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a width property to the .container class to test how the grid responds to different container sizes.

steps.title: Compare auto-fit with auto-fill
steps.instruction: In your .container class, temporarily change the grid-template-columns property from using auto-fit to auto-fill in the repeat() function.
steps.hint: Look for the repeat() function in grid-template-columns and replace 'auto-fit' with 'auto-fill'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid layout will now use auto-fill instead of auto-fit, which will create empty columns when the container width increases beyond what's needed for the grid items.
successCriteria: The grid-template-columns property uses repeat(auto-fill, minmax(100px, 1fr)) instead of auto-fit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're changing the keyword inside the repeat() function from 'auto-fit' to 'auto-fill'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're modifying the grid-template-columns property in the .container class and replacing 'auto-fit' with 'auto-fill'.

steps.title: Create a complete responsive grid layout example
steps.instruction: Update the .container class to use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)) for grid-template-columns to create a more spacious responsive grid.
steps.hint: Change the minmax() values in grid-template-columns from minmax(100px, 1fr) to minmax(250px, 1fr).
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid layout will now have columns that are at least 250px wide, creating a more spacious and practical responsive design.
successCriteria: The .container class has grid-template-columns set to repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you changed the minmax() values to minmax(250px, 1fr) in grid-template-columns.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you updated the grid-template-columns property correctly. It should be repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)).
